source: Cached georeferenced OS London five-foot 1893 mosaic; original Goad F3 for Crown/Johnson context; western approach reviewed on OS alone because Goad F16 is not cached
review: Re-read the complete unmodified OS mosaic. The southern Marshgate arm previously ran through Crown/Johnson instead of the public street east of its walls. Follow that street and keep the last two mill approach controls and the separate northern arm. At the ornamental moulding shed, Three Mills Lane follows the middle of the mapped street a little south of the former western bridge approach. Retain both 7 m carriageways and ordinary 1.1 m shoulders. No building clearance exception, new road link, or river change is introduced.

roads.name: Marshgate Lane

priorBridgeSpans.evidence: Provisional connection where the 1893 road trace meets the independently registered GIS bank. Deck versus culvert and exact bank alignment unresolved; not evidence of a documented named bridge.

bridgeSpans.evidence: Provisional connection where the 1893 road trace meets the independently registered GIS bank. Deck versus culvert and exact bank alignment unresolved; not evidence of a documented named bridge. Existing provisional crossing moved onto the mapped eastern lane; both endpoints relocated, with one intervening road control to follow its bend. Identity, deck style, 1.5 m height and uncertainty retained. Exact bank alignment and deck versus culvert remain unresolved.
bridgeSpans.heightEvidence: Task A (5 October 2026): no OS height on the crossing itself. The deck is laid level at the lane level the OS gives at its middle: Marshgate Lane reads 2.65 m at the High Street corner (sh_538078_183283, 5.7 m along the lane) and 3.19 m south of the deck (sh_538054_183338, 67.0 m along), and the deck spans 25.0-50.6 m along the lane, so linear interpolation gives 2.82-3.05 m, 2.93 m at its middle. The prior 1.5 m was an estimate that left the lane cut 1.7 m below its OS level (T22 decision 4). Deck versus culvert remains unresolved.

roads.name: Three Mills Lane

priorBridgeSpans.evidence: Mapped crossing; structural family from Victoria County History Essex VI pp57–61. Span proportions and levels are estimates.

bridgeSpans.evidence: Mapped crossing; structural family from Victoria County History Essex VI pp57–61. Span proportions and levels are estimates. Only the western endpoint of the existing Lea bridge moves onto the re-read approach; eastern endpoint, identity, deck style, single arch and 2.2 m estimated height retained.
bridgeSpans.heightEvidence: T22 (October 2026): deck height 4.23 m is the OS five-foot spot height on Three Mills Bridge, 21.2 ft (sh_538259_182802, setting bridge, data/maps/os-ground-levels.json), converted with the project datum. The prior 2.2 m was an estimate; with the terrace drawn at its OS levels the west approach (Three Mills Lane, OS 23.8 ft = 5.02 m 40 m west of the deck) would otherwise fall 2.8 m into a cutting to reach it. The bench mark at the west abutment (19.5 ft = 3.70 m) is cut on the abutment below the deck. Deck length, route and form unchanged.

bridgeSpans.evidence: Task D (October 2026). Mapped: on the OS five-foot plan (1893-96) the House Mill race runs under the mill and under Three Mills Lane to the River Lea, and the lane runs on unbroken between the mill and the river wall, with no parapet or railing drawn. The reviewed passage (core_river_connections.py, 'three-mills') crosses the lane centreline at (-598.8, 395.7). Interpreted: a flat slab over the race, carrying the 7 m carriageway and both 1.1 m footways flush with the street (no parapets), 7 m along the lane so it bears about 2 m beyond each side of the 3 m display passage. Construction, slab depth and abutments are estimates.
bridgeSpans.heightEvidence: Deck height 2.706 m is the OS five-foot spot height on the lane at the race, 16.2 ft (sh_538304_182814, 'Three Mills Lane east of the bridge', data/maps/os-ground-levels.json), converted with the project datum. Task C culverted the race under the lane instead (no deck); that cut the back rivers off from the Lea and left the lane sagging to about 0.9 m over the race.

roads.bridgeReview: Only the western endpoint of the existing Lea bridge moves onto the re-read approach; eastern endpoint, identity, deck style, single arch and 2.2 m estimated height retained.
